core_meaning.meaning_explanation: Haatim corresponds to the Arabic form حاتم (Arabic حاتم (Ḥātim); from the root ح ت م 'to decide'). Its core sense is generous giver, open-handed. Haatim is Arabic حاتم (Ḥātim). Its currency comes overwhelmingly from Ḥātim al-Ṭāʾī, the pre-Islamic Arab paragon of generosity, so that 'Ḥātim' functions almost as a byword for an open-handed giver. The source gloss 'the giver' reflects that association rather than a lexical meaning of the root (which means 'to judge, decide, make obligatory').
